approach: Add an `athena.focus/1` record (new AnyRecord variant, path records/focus/<month>/<id>.json, fields id, at, text, set_by), loaded into `Records.focus`; the latest by id is the current focus. `Athena::set_focus` and `current_focus` in reading.rs back the new `athena focus [text]` command, and `StatusView.focus` makes `athena status` print it. For the caps, add a `[priority_caps]` section (urgent = 3, high = 10) to the schema and athena.toml. The cap logic is pure code in plan.rs: a `PriorityCaps` value (the two numbers plus a map of job id to the time of its latest person-written priority record) goes to a new `Plan::build_capped`. `build_with` stays as a wrapper with no caps, so existing callers and tests are untouched. After `effective_priorities`, `build_capped` demotes the excess in memory and stores a `Demotion` per item in `Plan.demoted`. `priority_violations` uses the demoted tiers so it does not flag the demotion. The drain's `prepare` (which `athena plan` and `drain` share) gets the caps from a new `Steps::priority_caps` method. Its default is "no caps", so the many fake `Steps` impls compile unchanged, and `RealSteps` overrides it from athena.toml and the records. `display::plan` prints one line per demotion. No request or priority record is written during planning.

decisions.choice: Do the capping inside Plan::build_capped on the effective (dependency-raised) tiers, and keep the result in Plan.demoted. Do not edit PlanEntry.priority.
decisions.reason: The request says the cap applies to the effective priorities. Rewriting entry.priority would be undone when a dependent raises a prerequisite, and it would show the demoted tier in the entry's `priority` line. Keeping Plan.demoted next to the order lets priority_violations and the printout use the same tiers.

rejected.why: It misses the dependency raising in effective_priorities and mutates the entries callers print.

rejected.option: Add a priority_set_at field to PlanEntry
rejected.why: About 12 struct literals in drain.rs, tests/drain.rs and plan.rs would need editing. A side map in PriorityCaps avoids that.

decisions.choice: Take the caps and the person-set times through a new defaulted trait method `Steps::priority_caps(&self) -> PriorityCaps`. RealSteps overrides it by reading `config.priority_caps` from JobConfig and, for each job with priority records, the `at` of the highest-n record.
decisions.reason: `prepare` has no access to config or records except through Steps. A default of no caps leaves every fake Steps in the tests compiling and behaving as before. Only a person-written priority record counts as 'set by a person'; a `Priority:` line in the request text does not.

rejected.why: The plan module is pure data and deterministic code, so it should not read config.
It would force edits to about 10 fake impls, including in tests/drain.rs, which is not a deliverable.

decisions.choice: Keep order inside a capped tier: items with a person's priority record first, newest `at` first, then the rest by (rung, age). That is the sort build_with already applies within a wave. Urgent excess drops to high, and the high tier (including those just demoted) is then capped, with excess going to normal. Each demoted item gets exactly one Demotion with its final from and to tiers.
decisions.reason: This follows the accepted reading and reuses the existing ordering. Only items currently in the capped tier are lowered. An item a person set to normal or low is never raised or touched, so the record still wins for its item.

rejected.option: Rank the rest by age alone
rejected.why: The existing within-wave order is rung and then age, and 'plan order' should match it.

decisions.choice: Name the config section `[priority_caps]` with `urgent = 3` and `high = 10`, as a `#[serde(default)]` struct with deny_unknown_fields. Reset it in Config::reading_inputs and add it to the existing reading_inputs test.
decisions.reason: It matches how `[parallel]` is done, so old configs without the section still parse. Without the reset in reading_inputs, adding the section would change every reading's config digest.

rejected.why: They are unrelated settings, and [budget] fields feed the reading digest.

decisions.choice: Take `set_by` from `Git::config_get("user.name")` (exists in crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs). Refuse with a clear error if it is empty. Latest focus means the greatest record id.
decisions.reason: Priority records carry no identity, so git's user.name is the available source. Ids are time-ordered, and the focus record validates that text and set_by are non-empty.

rejected.why: The environment is not reliably set or recorded, and git already names the committer.

decisions.choice: This is not a refusal or matching rule, so no refusal_corpus case is added or changed. The cap demotes tiers and refuses nothing, and Priority::from_text and the request format are untouched.
decisions.reason: The brief's three-part corpus requirement applies only to rules that refuse or match input.

risks.risk: A PlanEntry or Plan literal elsewhere breaks when Plan gains the `demoted` field.
risks.mitigation: Plan derives Default, so any literal can use ..Default::default(). The producer compiles the workspace and fixes the few sites. PlanEntry is not changed at all.

risks.risk: Adding [priority_caps] changes every reading's config digest and invalidates stored readings.
risks.mitigation: Reset it in Config::reading_inputs like [parallel] and assert in the existing reading_inputs test that a changed cap leaves the text equal.

risks.risk: Demotion makes priority_violations report a false contradiction in the drain.
risks.mitigation: priority_violations applies Plan.demoted to the effective tiers before comparing, and the criterion 3 unit test asserts it returns empty.

risks.risk: Two focus records written in the same second get ambiguous order.
risks.mitigation: The record id carries a counter after the timestamp (RecordId::from_parts(at, n)). set_focus picks n above any existing id with the same timestamp, and the criterion 2 test sets both in quick succession.

risks.risk: The test harness cannot reach the fake-agent path for the end-to-end plan test, since `real_steps`, StubPage and RecordingLander are local to tests/drain.rs.
risks.mitigation: Criterion 3's end-to-end layer uses a fake Steps in drain.rs's own tests module (the Stub pattern). focus.rs uses only the binary and the common Fixture.

risks.risk: A demonstration command that the verifier may not run, since the allowed list names cargo, git and ls only.
risks.mitigation: Every demonstration is a cargo command. The grep in criteria 5 and 7 is a content check that the verifier can do with Grep; the cargo tests carry the behavior.

demonstrations.method: Integration test in crates/athena-cli/tests/focus.rs. It builds a Fixture (tests/common, exists), runs the real `athena` binary via CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena with current_dir = fx.root() and ATHENA_STATE_DIR = fx.state.path(), as tests/review.rs does, and asserts on the output and the files.
demonstrations.observes: `athena focus "speed first"` exits 0. A file appears under records/focus/<month>/ in the fixture repo and parses as an athena.focus/1 record with text "speed first" and a non-empty set_by. `athena focus` stdout contains "speed first", and `athena status` stdout contains it too.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no focus command, status field or record path, the first invocation exits non-zero (unknown subcommand), no file exists, and the stdout assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the `athena focus` and `athena status` binary commands, which call Athena::set_focus / current_focus (step 5) and StatusView.focus rendered by display::status. Seam: the fixture repo and ATHENA_STATE_DIR env, as in review.rs. Fixture sets git user.name. The fixture exists today; the focus code is added by steps 3-8.

demonstrations.method: Second test in tests/focus.rs. It runs `athena focus "speed first"`, then `athena focus "quality first"`, and reads the output of `athena focus` and `athena status`. It also counts the files under records/focus/.
demonstrations.observes: Both outputs contain "quality first" and do not contain "speed first". Two record files exist, so the earlier one is replaced by order and not deleted. If the two runs fall in the same second, the record id's counter part still orders them.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the current focus were the first record, the oldest, or an unordered pick, the outputs would still show "speed first" and the test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Same binary and Fixture seam as criterion 1. Records::load collects `focus` and the current one is the max id (steps 4-5). Needs the fixture only, which exists.

demonstrations.method: Two layers. (a) Pure unit test in crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs on `Plan::build_capped` with 5 complete entries at Urgent and a PriorityCaps { urgent: 3, high: 10, person_set } naming one of them. (b) A test in drain.rs's tests module using a test Steps impl that overrides `priority_caps` like the existing `Stub` does for caps/queue. It runs `drain::plan(&steps, ..)` and renders `display::plan(&report)`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core plan:: && cargo test -p athena-cli demotes
demonstrations.observes: (a) Counting `plan.demoted`, exactly 2 of the 5 ids are demoted from Urgent to High and 3 remain urgent. The person-set id is not among the demoted. The order lists the 3 urgent ids first. The person-set one is first of its tier, and the others follow in (rung, age) order. priority_violations on the result is empty. (b) The printed plan contains exactly 2 lines containing "demoted", one naming each demoted id, and the entries' own priority line is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without capping, plan.demoted is empty, all 5 count as urgent and no demotion lines print, so both assertions fail. If the person-set item were not preferred, a test that sets the newest-aged item as person-set would see it demoted.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: Plan::build_capped (added in step 2) and drain::plan, which calls Drain::prepare. Fixtures: plain PlanEntry values via the existing `entry` helpers in plan.rs and drain.rs tests, and a fake Steps whose `priority_caps` returns a PriorityCaps value (the default method is added in step 6). The capping logic lives in build_capped, not in the fake, which only supplies the numbers and the timestamps.

open_questions: Does the records gate (athena-gate records / RecordSet, not read here) keep an allow-list of directories under records/ that must also gain `focus`? That file is not in the brief's list. The producer should grep for where records/ paths are classified. If a change there is needed, it is a further deliverable, so say so.

Same question for the file scope: drain.rs (src) is needed for the wiring but is not among the expected deliverables. If the scope check refuses it, the wiring has no other place, since only `prepare` calls Plan::build_with for `athena plan` and `drain`.

Four person-set urgent items over a cap of 3: the plan as written demotes the oldest-set one, since 'extra items' includes them and the request orders person-set items first rather than exempting them. The assumption 'never demoted below their own record' could mean an exemption instead. Confirm which is meant.

An urgent item pushed out of the high tier after being demoted lands at normal, two tiers below its original, with one printed line. This follows the accepted reading (demoted items count toward the high cap). If 'one tier lower' is meant strictly, the high pass would skip them.
A kept urgent item's prerequisite may be demoted below it. This is harmless for order (dependencies still come first) but the printed tier differs. It is not handled specially.
Whether the focus record's directory needs a month shard: copy the shard format from the nearest month-sharded record's path arm in records.rs; the exact format was not read.
